PROJECT PLANNING

Ground Investigation: Ask What Decision the Information Must Support

Connect investigation planning with the project’s real uncertainties.

In this insight

Investigation is a decision-enabling activityShare the developing project geometrySeparate data from interpretationTurn gaps into planned actionsFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Investigation is a decision-enabling activity

Ground information supports the assessment of possible construction approaches, but the required information depends on the project. A client should ask the geotechnical team what decisions the proposed investigation is intended to support. This helps distinguish essential questions from general data collection. It also makes the commercial value clearer when an investigation request appears as an additional early-stage cost.

Share the developing project geometry

Investigation planning should have access to the current site boundaries, proposed excavation and relevant structural concept. Inform the specialists when these change. Information collected for an earlier or materially different scheme may need reassessment before it is relied on. The project manager’s role is to maintain that connection rather than assume a report remains sufficient because it has the correct site address.

Separate data from interpretation

Ask for a clear explanation of the observations, interpretations and remaining uncertainties. A useful report should help the relevant designers understand the basis of its conclusions. Procurement teams should preserve the complete report and any limitations when sharing it with bidders. Extracting only selected pages can remove context and encourage inconsistent assumptions about the conditions to be encountered.

Turn gaps into planned actions

Where the team identifies insufficient information, record the consequence and the next step. Decide whether the gap prevents a decision or can be managed as an explicit preliminary assumption. Keep that status visible as the project advances. The objective is not to eliminate every uncertainty, which is rarely possible, but to make the remaining uncertainty understandable and appropriately addressed in design and procurement.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Link investigation to a defined decision.
  • Reassess information when the scheme changes.
  • Share complete reports with their limitations.
